findings.title: Webhook accepts any HTTP method
findings.body: The handler in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts never checks req.method, so a state-changing credential create/update can be triggered by GET, HEAD or any verb. That enables CSRF, caching and log exposure of the operation. It should reject everything except POST with 405.

findings.title: Uncaught validation/decryption exceptions return 500
findings.body: The webhook calls zod .parse on the body, then symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse on the encrypted keys with no try/catch or safeParse. Any bad payload, wrong encryption key, or non-JSON plaintext throws and Next.js returns 500 instead of 400, leaking internals and making client errors indistinguishable from server failures.

findings.title: findFirst overwrites arbitrary credential
findings.body: The webhook looks up an existing credential with findFirst by userId+appId and updates that one row. Users can have multiple credentials for the same appId (e.g. two Google accounts, team vs user). findFirst picks an arbitrary row, so a sync can overwrite the wrong account's key and leave duplicates, corrupting calendar/video access.

findings.title: Minimum token schema uses computed literal keys
findings.body: minimumTokenResponseSchema declares properties like [z.string().toString()]: z.number(). In JavaScript that evaluates to a literal key such as "[object Object]", not a catch-all. It does not accept arbitrary expiry fields and requires a nonsense property, so safeParse fails for valid sync-endpoint responses and every synced refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". It should use catchall/passthrough/record.

findings.title: Missing refresh_token replaced with dummy string
findings.body: When the parsed response has no refresh_token, the helper mutates it to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers that spread the result into the stored credential (office365, salesforce, zoom) then permanently overwrite the real refresh token with that dummy value, destroying the ability to refresh again. Missing tokens should be preserved from the old credential, not faked.

findings.title: Sync branch returns raw fetch Response incompatible with callers
findings.body: When credential sharing is enabled the helper returns a raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Google expects GaxiosResponse with .data, HubSpot expects a HubSpot token object, Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM expect an axios response with .data. Accessing .data, .accessToken or .expiresIn on a fetch Response yields undefined and crashes or stores garbage. The helper also sends URLSearchParams with no Content-Type, no auth, and never checks response.ok before returning.

findings.title: Stores SafeParse wrapper as credential key
findings.body: Google refresh calls parseRefreshTokenResponse which returns a SafeParse result { success, data/error }. The code stores that whole wrapper as prisma.credential.key instead of .data. The next load does googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) on { success, data } and fails, permanently bricking the Google credential after one synced refresh.

findings.title: Uses prisma without importing it
findings.body: Salesforce CalendarService calls prisma.credential.update to persist refreshed tokens, but the file has no import of prisma from @calcom/prisma. At runtime this throws ReferenceError: prisma is not defined, so every Salesforce operation that constructs a client crashes.

findings.title: Refresh status checked via statusText and runs unconditionally
findings.body: Salesforce getClient unconditionally POSTs to login.salesforce.com on every instantiation with no expiry check, adding latency and rate-limit risk. It then validates with response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok/status. statusText is unreliable and often empty with HTTP/2/fetch, so valid token responses can be rejected and errors missed.

findings.title: Passes credentialId as userId and mismatches axios/fetch shape
findings.body: Bigin refresh calls refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId) where credentialId is credential.id, but the third parameter is userId. The sync endpoint receives a credential ID as calcomUserId, and team credentials with null userId are incorrectly treated as syncable. When sync is enabled the helper returns a fetch Response with no .data, so the following tokenInfo.data.error access throws TypeError.

findings.title: Expects axios response but gets fetch Response when synced
findings.body: ZohoCRM refresh wraps an axios call with refreshOAuthTokens. With sync enabled the helper returns a fetch Response which has .json() not .data. The code then reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error and zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.access_token, which are undefined for a fetch Response, causing a TypeError and failure to persist the new token.

findings.title: Wrong appSlug sent to credential sync endpoint
findings.body: Zoom refresh passes "zoomvideo" as appSlug to the sync endpoint, but the app's real slug/appId is "zoom" as used in the callback and credential creation. The external endpoint will receive an unknown slug and cannot locate the user's Zoom tokens, so synced Zoom refresh never works.
